summary.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces raised FY27 bookings guidance to INR2,600-2,700 crore (70-75% YoY) after Q2 bookings of INR906 crore, more than double YoY.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 presales hit a record INR906 crore (vs INR432 crore in Q2 FY26), and H1 bookings reached INR1,338 crore, up 120% YoY. Revenue was INR475 crore for H1 (up 96%) and INR157 crore in Q2; H1 PAT was INR120 crore (about 4x) and Q2 PAT INR23 crore (up 25%). Management raised FY27 bookings guidance from INR2,100-2,200 crore to INR2,600-2,700 crore, kept the 22-25% EBITDA margin guidance, and signalled a strong likelihood of the upper end of the INR4,000-5,000 crore GDV addition guidance. Net debt fell to INR200 crore from INR215 crore in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: more than 2x vs INR432 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Arvind Sylva (Green Reserve, premium high-rise) booked over INR500 crore within 30 days, about 60% of inventory by value. Bengaluru contributed about 50% of H1 sales and crossed INR600 crore for the first time. Sarjapur Road high-rise added with about INR470 crore top-line potential, sold at about INR12,600/sq ft.

segments.name: Ahmedabad
segments.commentary: Launched one project in Q2; contributed about 70% of sales last year. Existing Gujarat projects contribute through sustenance sales.

segments.name: Mumbai (MMR)
segments.commentary: Entry planned in H2 FY27 with two projects in Goregaon, targeting premium homes at INR2.5-5 crore ticket size.

segments.name: Sustenance and plotting
segments.commentary: H1 sustenance sales about INR745 crore, already above full-year FY26 sustenance of about INR600 crore; currently running at about INR300 crore per quarter. Plotting portfolio continues to contribute.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings guidance raised to INR2,600-2,700 crore (70-75% YoY) from INR2,100-2,200 crore (35-40% growth).
Business development GDV addition guidance of INR4,000-5,000 crore for FY27; strong likelihood of the upper end. Cumulative FY27 BD added is about INR3,100 crore as of September 2026.
EBITDA margin guidance of about 22-25% reiterated; management said it is the underwriting basis, with actual margins running higher.
Long-term growth guidance of about 30% YoY; management said FY27 is a reset year and that sustaining 30% on the higher base should not be very challenging.

H2 FY27 launches: about 4 projects (two in Mumbai, two in Bengaluru) worth INR2,200-2,500 crore booking value, likely late Q3 or in Q4 subject to final approvals. Originally about 6 launches guided for FY27; 2 done in H1 (about INR1,250 crore inventory).

Medium term: target about INR5,000 crore of presales reachable; vertical share to rise from 35% to 65% over about 4 years (portfolio currently 65:35 horizontal:vertical). Target JD:outright mix of 70:30 by GDV over the medium term.
Annual land outflow of about INR1,000 crore is considered comfortable; a fourth market is likely only in about 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Unrealised operating cash flow from existing pipeline estimated at INR5,197 crore.
Net operating cash flow of INR152 crore in Q2 and INR233 crore in H1 FY27.
Construction spend has more than doubled YoY; management did not give specific construction outflow numbers, and said delivery should reflect this over time.
Debt-to-equity about 0.26, with HDFC platform available for additional funding.
Inventory on balance sheet about INR2,700 crore, mostly construction and overhead spend on JD projects, with many projects nearing completion.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings split: about 65% from new launches and 35% from sustenance.
Arvind Sylva (Bengaluru) booked over INR500 crore in 30 days, about 60% of inventory by value.
Mumbai positioning: premium homes at INR2.5-5 crore ticket size, not super-luxury or affordable; pricing to be set close to launch with partner feedback, aiming for a premium but competitive price.
Management said it underwrites on current prices and not on price escalation; inflation and contingency buffers added over the last 1-1.5 years are expected to absorb the recent commodity cost rise.
Management acknowledged a sharp cost escalation in the last 6 months from geopolitical factors (West Asia, crude) and said the company may be on the more advanced side of the cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What launches are planned for H2 FY27, and in which markets and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Four projects worth INR2,200-2,500 crore: two in Mumbai and two in Bengaluru. Timing depends on final approvals, so the launches may land in late Q3 or in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 22-25% EBITDA margin when reported margins are much higher?
qa_highlights.answer: The guidance is the underwriting basis for new projects. Past price growth and cost control have lifted margins above guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD and balance sheet be managed while growing about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Target 70:30 JD:outright mix by GDV over the medium term, with headroom from a debt-to-equity of 0.26 and an HDFC platform. Land outflow of about INR1,000 crore per year is considered comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory breakdown and sustainable margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of about INR2,700 crore is mainly construction and overhead spend, with a small land component. Management said Q1 was boosted by one project's revenue recognition and Q2 PAT margin was about 14%, in line with guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How does management ensure project handover timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction outflows are tracked by project and region, with daily operations monitoring and senior governance. Construction spend has more than doubled YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How will sustenance sales shift from launch-led presales?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustenance is now about INR300 crore per quarter after a target of INR200 crore per quarter was set around Q4 FY26. More launches in all three markets are expected to make it a larger part of the mix.

risks_watch: H2 launches are subject to final approvals and may slip from Q3 to Q4, which would shift presales into the year-end.
Mumbai entry is new for the brand, with strong competition from large developers and a premium price point (INR2.5-5 crore tickets).
Cost inflation from geopolitical factors and commodity prices, plus a possibly advanced real estate cycle.
Management did not quantify construction spend, and it is unclear how quickly the doubling in construction outflow will reflect in deliveries.
Achieving the 70% to 30% JD:outright target and the INR4,000-5,000 crore BD target while managing capital allocation.
Presales growth of about 30% from the higher FY27 base needs to be sustained; management described FY27 as a reset year.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on bookings, guidance upgrade and sustenance momentum. Measured and careful on margins, capital discipline and the cycle; management declined to give specific construction spend or delivery numbers.
key_quotes: Our performance in H1 FY '27 has been encouraging with bookings of INR1,338 crores, registering a growth of 120% on a year -on-year basis.
The second quarter of FY '27 has been a very strong one for Arvind SmartSpaces with the company recording its highest ever quarterly presales and collections performance.
So we feel quite confident that we should be able to get our guidance of about INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores in the current year.
So we are not really dependent on price increase to be able to manage our P&L.

growth.why: FY27 bookings guidance raised to INR2,600-2,700 crore (70-75% YoY) on Q2 presales of INR906 crore and Arvind Sylva selling about 60% of inventory in 30 days, but the H2 launches (INR2,200-2,500 crore, about 4 projects) are slipping to late Q3 or Q4 subject to approvals, and no construction or capacity numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated 22-25% EBITDA margin guidance as an underwriting basis, with actual margins running higher; Q2 PAT margin about 14% and Q2 EBITDA up 46% YoY, though a sharp 6-month commodity cost rise and an advanced cycle cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Construction spend has more than doubled YoY but no numbers were given; four H2 launches (INR2,200-2,500 crore) are subject to approvals and may slip to Q4, and Mumbai is a new market entry planned in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 bookings guided to INR2,600-2,700 crore (70-75% YoY) after H1 bookings of INR1,338 crore (up 120%), with sustenance running about INR300 crore per quarter; but H2 needs about INR1,350-1,500 crore of launch bookings to hit the range, and that depends on approvals.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is largely asset-light via JD projects, with debt-to-equity about 0.26, HDFC funding headroom and annual land outflow of about INR1,000 crore called comfortable; no new capex plant was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Bookings guidance was already raised to INR2,600-2,700 crore and management signalled a strong likelihood of the upper end of the INR4,000-5,000 crore BD target, but upside depends on H2 launch timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 launches (about 4 projects, INR2,200-2,500 crore) may slip from late Q3 to Q4 on approvals, which would push presales into year-end, and cost inflation from crude and geopolitics is a risk to the margin cushion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 4 projects worth INR2,200-2,500 crore are planned (two in Mumbai at INR2.5-5 crore tickets, two in Bengaluru), subject to final approvals; 2 of 6 planned FY27 launches are done.

rows.label: Mumbai (MMR) entry with two Goregaon projects
rows.why: Entry planned in H2 FY27 at INR2.5-5 crore tickets, a new market for the brand facing strong large-developer competition.

rows.label: Sustenance sales at about INR300 crore per quarter
rows.why: H1 sustenance of about INR745 crore already exceeds FY26's about INR600 crore, and the run-rate is about INR300 crore per quarter, with more launches expected to lift it further.

rows.label: Net debt reduction and JD-led BD funding
rows.why: Net debt fell to INR200 crore from INR215 crore in Q2, debt-to-equity is about 0.26, and the 70:30 JD:outright target limits balance-sheet strain while BD adds about INR3,100 crore cumulatively.

tone.note: Management was confident on bookings, the guidance raise, Arvind Sylva sales and sustenance momentum, but cautious on margins, the advanced cycle, cost inflation and construction spend, which it did not quantify; analysts pushed on the margin gap versus guidance and delivery timing.
